name: Alloy: Delvesmith
pitch: A top-down pixel-art action RPG. Each hero binds two of six elements, and every pair reacts both ways: fire on nature sets off Combust, frost then earth Shatters. You build your moves at the Anvil as chains of up to five, each with its own form, elements and rune sockets.

art.alt: A pixel-art hero swings a greatsword at a hulking foreman in a mine lit by molten cracks.

press.description: Alloy: Delvesmith is a top-down pixel-art action RPG built by one developer. Each hero binds two of six elements, and every pair of elements reacts, both ways. Moves are items you build at the Anvil: chains of up to five, each with its own form, elements and rune sockets. It is in development and playable in the browser during playtesting.
features: Six elements, and every pair reacts both ways: fire on nature sets off Combust, frost then earth Shatters.
Build your own moves at the Anvil: chains of up to five, each with its own form, elements and rune sockets.
Bosses with scripted phases and break gauges.
Playable now in the browser while in playtest.

name: Unhappy Campers
hook: You forgot the tent stakes. The raccoons did not forget your truck keys.
pitch: A 2–4 player physics co-op camping trip that goes wrong in three acts. Pack late, camp badly, then hike out in the dark after the raccoons take the truck. One run takes about an hour.

art.alt: Two campers carrying a big red cooler between them trip over each other in the middle of camp.

press.description: Unhappy Campers is a co-op camping trip for 2–4 players (up to 6 in clown-car lobbies) that goes wrong in three acts: you pack late, you camp badly, and then raccoons steal your truck and you hike out in the dark. Required gear, poisonous berries and the rules of the night change every run, so players learn by eating, guessing and arguing.
features: Three acts in one run: a packing scramble at home, a day making camp, and a night hike out after the raccoons take the truck.
Nature is petty, then dangerous: squirrels and raccoons steal by day, bears are real danger, and cryptids own the night.
The rules change every run: required items, poisonous berries and cryptid rules are randomized.
Everything you do earlier pays off later: what you pack feeds camp, and camp feeds the escape.
A full run fits in about an hour, and a failed run should be funny, not a waste of time.

clips.caption: A raccoon pops up behind the cooler.
A squirrel drops out of a tree onto a camper.
Two campers throw the third off the dock.
The big cooler takes two people. One of them trips.
A barefoot sprint ends at the raccoon log.
A raccoon goes through a knocked-out camper's fanny pack.
Four campers play dead at once.
Pitching the tent without the stakes.

name: Two Minute Empire
hook: Two minutes to turn a Hut into a Palace.
pitch: A two-minute merge puzzle on an 89-hex island, made for a phone held upright. Three alike that touch merge into the next tier, up a ladder of seven from Hut to Palace, and every building pays gold each second. Each reign starts from a 45-card deck, so where you put the pieces matters more than how fast you tap.

art.alt: Seven hexes of a low-poly island in a dark night sea: a gold-domed palace at the centre, with a castle, a walled city, smaller settlements, a forest and a farm with a windmill around it.

press.description: Two Minute Empire is a 120-second merge puzzle built by one developer. Players place pieces from a 45-card deck on an 89-hex island: three or more touching alike merge into the next of seven tiers, from Hut to Palace, and every building pays gold each second. As settlements grow they want Food, then Trade, then Faith, paid for with Lumber and Stone from nearby Forests and Quarries, and a settlement with every need met pays double. It is free to play in the browser, made for a phone held upright, and in playtest.
features: Three or more touching alike merge into the next tier on the hex you placed, and the result can merge again: chains pay ×3, ×10 and ×30 gold.
Seven tiers from Hut to Palace, each paying about five times the one below: a Hut earns 1 gold a second, a Palace 15,000.
Villages and bigger push your borders into the fog (a Village by 1 hex, a Town by 2, a City by 3), where more Forests, Quarries and gold veins wait.
Settlements with every need met thrive: they pay double and count double in merges, so a served district grows from pairs.
Four peoples, each with its own deck: Heartland build anywhere, Mariners fish and trade from the coast, Woodfolk hunt and worship beside Forests, and Stoneborn build in stone and mine Boulders.
A daily island, the same for everyone, that rotates through the four peoples, and a link to share any other island.

clips.caption: A Banner becomes a Village and chains four steps up to the Palace. The last step pays ×30: 4,500,000 gold.
A Temple brings Faith to a City, so it thrives and pays double.
Thriving settlements count double in merges: two Villages make a Town, and it chains into a City.
The first Castle pauses the clock for a draft: one card of three goes on top of the deck.
The clock hits 0:00 and the reign is tallied into a grade.
